scenarios.title: Build a reliable report-mode interface
scenarios.summary: Validate an operation before choosing a read-only report.
scenarios.objective:
Build a card interface. brief LABEL and full LABEL each require exactly two arguments and a nonempty LABEL. --help or -h alone prints Usage: card brief|full LABEL followed by a line break and returns 0. Any other mode, missing/extra argument or empty label prints that same usage line only to standard error and returns 2.

For brief, print Card: LABEL and Summary: SUMMARY, each followed by a line break. For full, print those same lines, then Details: and a line break, then the exact contents of details.txt. SUMMARY is supplied, and LABEL and SUMMARY may contain spaces, percent signs or wildcard-looking text. Successful cards return 0 with no error output. Leave every virtual file unchanged. Use the supplied filenames exactly.

initial.source:
# Build the full argument interface and both report views.
printf 'Card: %s\nSummary: %s\n' "$2" "$SUMMARY"

cases.name: A full card preserves an unterminated detail
cases.stdout:
Card: South desk
Summary: Two checks
Details:
Rack B
100% complete

cases.name: Keep the whole label and summary literal
cases.stdout:
Card: *.txt 100% ready
Summary: Line one
Line two

cases.name: A spaced unknown mode is one value
Help must not ignore extra arguments

solution:
case "$1" in
    --help|-h)
        if test "$#" -ne 1; then
            printf 'Usage: card brief|full LABEL\n' >&2
            exit 2
        fi
        printf 'Usage: card brief|full LABEL\n'
        exit 0
        ;;
esac
if test "$#" -ne 2 || test -z "$2"; then
    printf 'Usage: card brief|full LABEL\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
case "$1" in
    brief) printf 'Card: %s\nSummary: %s\n' "$2" "$SUMMARY" ;;
    full)
        printf 'Card: %s\nSummary: %s\nDetails:\n' "$2" "$SUMMARY"
        cat details.txt
        ;;
    *) printf 'Usage: card brief|full LABEL\n' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect argument count and mode first, then quoting and exact line breaks. A valid view must not touch files.
scenarios.explanation: The interface separates help, ordinary argument validation and exact mode selection. A default arm gives unknown modes a real error path. Whole outcomes test output, status and unchanged files; equivalent supported conditionals are accepted.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use the argument checks, quoted printing and statuses from “Preview or publish a batch investigation safely”. This lesson adds a clear multi-way decision.

concepts.title: Choose the first matching arm
concepts.text: case "$1" in starts a decision using the entire first argument. A pattern ends at ), its commands follow, and ;; finishes that arm. The first match wins; later arms do not run. End the decision with esac. Patterns separated by | choose the same commands, such as quick|summary).

concepts.title: An explicit default is part of the interface
concepts.text: Use *) as the final arm for everything else. Print a useful diagnostic to standard error and choose a nonzero exit status. Check help separately before ordinary argument counts when help has a different interface. No-match alone returns 0; it is not an error handler.

concepts.title: Patterns and values have different roles
concepts.text: The selector stays one value, even if it contains spaces or wildcard-looking text. In patterns, unquoted * matches any number of bytes and ? one byte; quoting either makes it literal. quick* is a broad pattern; 'quick*' expects a literal star. Use exact mode names here. When printing a label, quote it and use a fixed printf format.

concepts.title: Keep the workbench boundary clear
concepts.text: Patterns here support simple * and ? with C/POSIX byte matching. A byte is not necessarily a whole UTF8 character. Bracket patterns such as [ab] and fallthrough operators ;& and ;;& are outside this workbench; use ;;. These limits do not restrict quoted literal text.

concepts.title: Recognize the test command spelling
concepts.text: test -z "$2" is the same empty-text check as [ -z "$2" ]. With test, omit the closing ]; the options and success statuses are the same. test "$#" -ne 2 checks whether the supplied argument count differs from two. As in earlier guards, A || B tries B only after A fails, so either invalid check can select the error branch. The example uses this spelling before its new case decision.

teaching.inputs: Arguments are quick and Gallery desk. NOTE is Map catalog; museum.txt belongs only to this example. The assignment uses different modes, variables and files.
teaching.try_change: Replace only quick|summary with 'quick*' in the first pattern and Run. The literal star no longer matches quick, so the default reports Unknown view. Restore the original patterns to repair it.

scenarios.title: Route a prioritized work list without losing records
scenarios.summary: Apply ordered routes, preserve records and finish an audit after errors.
scenarios.objective:
One argument names an existing work-list file. Its supplied filename differs from priority.txt and regular.txt. Replace priority.txt and regular.txt with the routed records, in input order, one complete record per line. ship:urgent:TEXT goes to priority; other ship:TEXT and collect:TEXT go to regular. TEXT must be nonempty; ship:, collect: and ship:urgent: are rejected. The supplied records have no leading or trailing spaces or tabs; spaces inside a record are text. Blank records and hold: records are ignored. Every other record is rejected. Keep each supplied record, including its prefix and internal spaces, exactly; do not split or interpret it.

Continue after rejection, printing Cannot route: RECORD and a line break to standard error for each rejected record, in order. Print Priority: N, Regular: N, Ignored: N and Rejected: N to standard output, each on its own line. Include a final record without a line break. Return 1 if anything was rejected, otherwise 0. Leave the input and every other supplied file unchanged. Use the supplied filenames exactly.

initial.source:
# Route and count every record; keep a complete rejection audit.
: > priority.txt
: > regular.txt
while read -r record || test -n "$record"; do
    printf '%s\n' "$record" >> regular.txt
done < "$1"
printf 'Priority: 0\nRegular: 0\nIgnored: 0\nRejected: 0\n'

cases.name: Continue after several rejected records
cases.stderr:
Cannot route: ship:
Cannot route: unknown:Box
Cannot route: ship:urgent:

cases.name: Blank and held records are ignored
Empty input still clears old outputs
Spaces percent signs wildcards and colons stay literal
Append each routed record after one initial clear

solution:
: > priority.txt
: > regular.txt
priority=0
regular=0
ignored=0
rejected=0
while read -r record || test -n "$record"; do
    case "$record" in
        ship:|collect:|ship:urgent:) printf 'Cannot route: %s\n' "$record" >&2; rejected=$((rejected+1)) ;;
        ship:urgent:*) printf '%s\n' "$record" >> priority.txt; priority=$((priority+1)) ;;
        ship:*|collect:*) printf '%s\n' "$record" >> regular.txt; regular=$((regular+1)) ;;
        ''|hold:*) ignored=$((ignored+1)) ;;
        *) printf 'Cannot route: %s\n' "$record" >&2; rejected=$((rejected+1)) ;;
    esac
done < "$1"
printf 'Priority: %s\nRegular: %s\nIgnored: %s\nRejected: %s\n' "$priority" "$regular" "$ignored" "$rejected"
if test "$rejected" -gt 0; then exit 1; fi
exit 0
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare route files as well as counts. A later urgent pattern cannot undo an earlier broad match. Rejection should not stop the batch.
scenarios.explanation: A record takes the first matching route. Specific and empty-payload decisions must precede broader forms; appending preserves records already routed. Counts and a continued rejection stream describe the entire batch. Equivalent supported loops and tests can produce the same outcomes.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use first-match/default decisions from “Build a reliable report-mode interface”, finite input from “Keep the final record when input ends”, and counters from “Number a handover queue”.

concepts.title: Put specific routes before broad ones
concepts.text: send:rush:* also matches send:*. Put the rush pattern first when it must take the fast lane. A later, more specific pattern does not override an earlier match. The complete record stays text; the pattern does not remove its prefix.

concepts.title: Preserve complete records while routing
concepts.text: By default, read -r removes spaces and tabs at the ends of a record, while keeping backslashes and internal spaces. These supplied records have no edge spaces or tabs, so quoted printf '%s\n' "$row" writes each complete record unchanged, including percent signs. while read -r row || test -n "$row" keeps a final record without a line break. A blank row is one empty value.

concepts.title: Clear once, append per record
concepts.text: Prepare each output once before reading the list, then append each routed record. Clearing inside the loop loses earlier work. Count the route actually taken. Decide explicitly which records are held and which are rejected, and keep processing when the task requires a complete audit.

teaching.example:
: > 'fast lane.txt'
: > 'normal lane.txt'
fast=0
normal=0
held=0
while read -r row || test -n "$row"; do
    case "$row" in
        send:rush:*) printf '%s\n' "$row" >> 'fast lane.txt'; fast=$((fast+1)) ;;
        send:*|return:*) printf '%s\n' "$row" >> 'normal lane.txt'; normal=$((normal+1)) ;;
        ''|hold:*) held=$((held+1)) ;;
        *) printf 'Unknown: %s\n' "$row" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done < 'museum queue.txt'
printf 'Fast: %s\nNormal: %s\nHeld: %s\n' "$fast" "$normal" "$held"
teaching.inputs: No arguments. museum queue.txt supplies three museum movements. The example writes fast lane.txt and normal lane.txt; keep.txt must stay intact. Like the assignment, these records have no leading or trailing spaces or tabs; this lets read -r preserve the supplied text. The supplied input filename differs from fast lane.txt and normal lane.txt.
teaching.try_change: Move the send:*|return:* arm before send:rush:* and Run. The frame takes the normal lane because the first match wins. Move the rush arm back first to repair the result.

scenarios.title: Preview or publish a validated release plan
scenarios.summary: Separate whole-plan validation from file publication and ledger updates.
scenarios.objective:
Accept exactly two arguments: preview|apply and a nonempty source filename. The supplied source filename differs from published.txt and ledger.txt. Otherwise print Usage: release preview|apply FILE only to standard error, with a line break, and return 2. If the source is absent, print Missing input: FILE to standard error with a line break and return 1. Neither failure may print normal output or change any file.

Read the complete source, including an unterminated final record. ready:TEXT with nonempty TEXT enters the plan as the whole record, in input order. The supplied records have no leading or trailing spaces or tabs; spaces inside a record are text. Blank and hold: records are ignored. At the first other record, print Bad entry: RECORD to standard error with a line break and return 1; print no plan and leave every file unchanged. The plan joins accepted records with line breaks inside, with none at the end.

A successful preview prints Plan: <PLAN> and a line break, changing no files. A successful apply replaces published.txt with exactly PLAN, appends Source: FILE and a line break to ledger.txt, and prints Applied: <PLAN> with a line break. This also applies to an empty plan. Return 0 with no error output; preserve the source and all other supplied files. Use the supplied filenames exactly.

initial.source:
# Validate every record before any publication or ledger change.
candidate=$(cat "$2")
case "$1" in
    preview) printf 'Plan: <%s>\n' "$candidate" ;;
    apply)
        printf '%s' "$candidate" > published.txt
        printf 'Source: %s\n' "$2" >> ledger.txt
        printf 'Applied: <%s>\n' "$candidate"
        ;;
esac

cases.name: Apply literal text from a spaced filename
An empty preview preserves existing files
Applying an all-held plan produces an empty file
Reject an empty ready label after valid data
Reject an unknown prefix before a preview
Quoted wildcard-looking filename and final record

solution:
if test "$#" -ne 2 || test -z "$2"; then
    printf 'Usage: release preview|apply FILE\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
case "$1" in
    preview|apply) : ;;
    *) printf 'Usage: release preview|apply FILE\n' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
if test -f "$2"; then :; else
    printf 'Missing input: %s\n' "$2" >&2
    exit 1
fi
build_plan() {
    while read -r record || test -n "$record"; do
        case "$record" in
            ''|hold:*) : ;;
            ready:?*) printf '%s\n' "$record" ;;
            *) printf 'Bad entry: %s\n' "$record" >&2; return 1 ;;
        esac
    done < "$1"
    return 0
}
candidate=$(build_plan "$2")
status=$?
if test "$status" -ne 0; then exit "$status"; fi
case "$1" in
    preview) printf 'Plan: <%s>\n' "$candidate" ;;
    apply)
        printf '%s' "$candidate" > published.txt
        printf 'Source: %s\n' "$2" >> ledger.txt
        printf 'Applied: <%s>\n' "$candidate"
        ;;
esac
scenarios.retry_guidance: Use the error path to test preservation. A partial candidate must not reach either preview or publication; a successful apply must append rather than replace the ledger.
scenarios.explanation: Preparation may print partial text before finding an error, so its status must be checked before any preview or file change. A successful candidate can be reviewed or published, and the ledger append is separate from replacing the publication. Behavior grading accepts supported alternatives, including variable buffering without capture or conditional dispatch without case.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use “Route a prioritized work list without losing records” and the captured-status checks from “Investigate findings without losing their status”. “Repair a review that damages its inputs” explains function variables and early return.

concepts.title: Validate the whole plan before publishing
concepts.text: A preview must not change publication files. Prepare a candidate in variables or captured text, and finish validation before replacing a file or appending the ledger. If a later record is invalid, earlier prepared text must not become a partial publication.

concepts.title: Capture output and status separately
concepts.text: text=$(prepare "$2") stores printed text. Read status=$? immediately: it tells you whether preparation succeeded. A diagnostic is not the status, and a later printf would replace $?. An ordinary helper return 1 is a recoverable validation result here. Exit before printing or saving a failed candidate.

concepts.title: Use a nonempty prefix match
concepts.text: ok:?* requires at least one byte after ok:. The final * allows the remaining text. An empty label falls through to the error arm. The wait:* arm skips held items. Empty lines have their own '' pattern. These prefixes belong to the example; the assignment uses ready: and hold:.

concepts.title: Choose review or save after validation
concepts.text: The example reviews the captured text without writes. The save arm replaces the docket and appends one ledger line. Capture removes line breaks at the end, keeping spaces and line breaks inside; the saved docket therefore has no final line break. Restoring the review action restores a read-only operation.

teaching.inputs: Arguments are review and requests.txt. The museum example has separate ok:/wait: records, a docket and loan ledger. Each Run starts with its own sample files; simulated file changes reset before the next run. Your script draft stays saved. The records have no leading or trailing spaces or tabs: read -r trims those edges by default, while retaining backslashes and internal spaces. The supplied input filename differs from docket.txt and loan ledger.txt.
teaching.try_change: Change only mode=$1 to mode=save and Run. Inspect the replaced docket and appended loan ledger. Restore mode=$1 to return to the read-only review.
